key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical neural network can improve sample efficiency for peptide-HLA binding prediction, especially when training data are scarce.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum-enhanced models may be useful for low-data bioinformatics and immunotherapy pipelines where accurate prediction matters but labeled data are limited.
method: Multi-source biological features encode peptide-HLA inputs.
Parallel quantum feature extractors learn compact representations.
A quantum-enhanced classifier combines extracted signals for binding prediction.
evidence_signal: Across two HLA alleles (A*02:01 and B*07:02), HQNN beat a parameter-matched classical CNN at all training sizes, with larger gains in smaller-data settings; ablations and noise-aware simulations supported the design.
watch_item: The reported benefits come from simulation on only two alleles, so broader validation and hardware-scale testing are still needed.
paper_title: Improving Sample Efficiency in Peptide-HLA Binding Prediction with Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Networks
